newsitem.title: USA: Foley, diplomats touted for key ambassadorships.
newsitem.headline: Foley, diplomats touted for key ambassadorships.

text.p: Former U.S. House Speaker Tom Foley is likely to be appointed U.S. ambassador to Japan and President Bill Clinton will nominate career diplomats to be ambassadors to Russia and Germany, a U.S. official said on Thursday.
The official, who asked not to be identified, said James Collins would be named to head the U.S. embassy in Moscow and John Kornblum was Clinton's choice to be his envoy to Bonn.
Collins was deputy chief of mission in Moscow during the turbulent times surrounding the collapse of the Soviet Union, and Kornblum has been deeply involved in efforts to achieve peace in Bosnia.
Foley, a 68-year-old former Democratic House of Representatives Speaker who represented a district in Washington State during his tenure in Congress, is currently with a top Washington law firm.

His wife, Heather, told Reuters on Thursday night she was unaware that Clinton had made a final decision on a replacement for former Vice President Walter Mondale, who resigned as U.S. ambassador to Japan last December.
